justifications.functional_suitability: Catalog Management Component (Spring Data JPA) and Circulation Component cover cataloguing and circulation. Search Service and Web Application's Catalogue & Search serve discovery. Digital items are weak: e-Book Vendors have no container integrating them, and digital cataloguing is not explicit.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Dedicated Elasticsearch Search Service, Query Cache Layer (Caffeine), Redis Cache, PgBouncer Connection Pooler, GIN indexes, client-side React Query caching, and rate limiting protect the 800 ms target. Gaps: no explicit scaling or replica mechanisms, and no load testing or measurement.
justifications.compatibility: Integrations use REST/OAuth2, HTTPS, gRPC and AMQP with the Payment Gateway and Notification Service. However, no container or component integrates e-Book Vendors, and the Enterprise Search Service is ambiguous alongside the internal Search Service. Technology labels for some relations are inconsistent.
justifications.usability: Patrons and Librarians both use the Web Application (React) with Router / Layout, Circulation & Self-Service and Catalogue & Search components, plus role-based access in Authentication. There are no distinct staff interfaces, accessibility or multilingual mechanisms, and notifications are only a background channel.
justifications.reliability: Notification Worker has a Retry & Dead-Letter Handler and Redis offers Cluster/Sentinel, and the database is ACID. There is no database replication, backup, failover, multi-instance deployment or health monitoring. The API Gateway, Search and Core Business Service are single points of failure.
justifications.security: API Gateway provides SSL/TLS Termination, Kong JWT/OAuth2 Authentication & Authorization and Rate Limiting. pgAudit Audit Logging Extension gives accountability, and the Compliance Sanitizer masks PII. EU residency is stated for Database and Search. Gaps: no encryption at rest, no secrets management, and unclear residency for the external services.
justifications.maintainability: Clear containers (API Gateway, Core Business Service, Search Service, Notification Worker) with focused components such as Catalog Management, Circulation and Payment Integration. The notification pipeline is well decomposed. Core Business Service is a monolith, and Redis is shared between gateway and cache.
justifications.portability: Standard open technologies (PostgreSQL, Redis, Elasticsearch, Kong/Nginx, Spring Boot) are replaceable and avoid vendor lock-in. However, no containerization, deployment or infrastructure-as-code elements are described, and no deployment environments are defined beyond the EU-only restriction.

sensitivity_points: Elasticsearch cluster sizing under 2,000 concurrent queries
Local Caffeine cache hit rate per instance
tradeoffs: Throttling protects P99 but may reject legitimate semester-start traffic
Local caches reduce latency but are inconsistent across instances
PERF-01.justification: Dedicated Elasticsearch, gateway routing, client and query caching suit the target. But no replicas, sizing, scaling or load-test evidence is given, and the throttling Redis is shared with the business cache. P99 is plausible but unproven.

sensitivity_points: Synchronous metadata sync adds indexing load during searches
Query cache TTL determines when changed items become visible
tradeoffs: Direct sync gives freshness but couples writes to search load
Query caching speeds searches but can delay visibility of updates
PERF-02.justification: Catalog Management synchronizes metadata to Search Service, so changes can become searchable. Reads and writes are not isolated, there is no async indexing queue, and cache invalidation is undefined. The 5-minute and P99 targets are plausible but not assured.

sensitivity_points: No stated Elasticsearch replicas or shards
Failover and health-check behaviour of routing component
tradeoffs: Separate search keeps circulation running but search stays a single point of failure
Postgres GIN index could serve as fallback but adds a second search path
AVAIL-01.justification: Circulation persists in PostgreSQL independent of search, so loans are not lost. But no search cluster, replication or failover is modelled, and no fallback is wired to the GIN index. Search outage handling is unaddressed.

sensitivity_points: Number of Web Application instances not specified
Session state handling and load balancer health checks
tradeoffs: Stateless SPA eases failover but depends on a redundant frontend hosting setup
Gateway load balancing helps but is itself a single entry point
AVAIL-02.justification: A React SPA is stateless and the gateway has load balancing, which hints at redundancy. But no multiple instances, deployment or failover mechanism for the portal is shown. Loan transactions are persisted in the database, so they are not lost.

sensitivity_points: No dedicated e-book integration component exists
Catalogue model must accommodate vendor-specific metadata
tradeoffs: Central Core service is simple but lacks isolation for new integrations
Adding vendor logic to Catalog Management raises coupling
MOD-01.justification: The e-book vendors appear at context level, but the container model has no relationship to them and no integration component or adapter abstraction. A new provider would touch Catalog Management and others, so changes are not confined to one component.

sensitivity_points: Loan rules likely embedded in Circulation Component code
No rules engine or configuration store
tradeoffs: Simple Spring transactions are easy to build but hardcode policy
Runtime configurability would require adding a rules or config mechanism
MOD-02.justification: No rules engine, configuration store or per-library policy mechanism is present. Loan rules reside in Circulation Component code, so different rules need code changes and redeployment. The architecture does not support runtime configuration.

sensitivity_points: External Notification Service and Payment Gateway location unspecified
No enforced deployment region or policy controls
tradeoffs: PII masking limits exposure but reduces notification personalisation
External SaaS integrations ease delivery but risk non-EU processing
SEC-01.justification: Database is EU-restricted and PII masking precedes notification dispatch. But EU residency of Redis, Elasticsearch, the gateway and external services is only asserted in descriptions, with no region pinning or preventive control. The data flow is not prevented by design.

sensitivity_points: Object-level ownership check not modelled in Core service
Application-level denial events are not logged; pgAudit logs only DB access
tradeoffs: Edge authentication offloads services but cannot enforce per-record authorization
pgAudit gives strong audit trails but misses denied application requests
SEC-02.justification: The gateway validates JWTs and the frontend has role-based access, but nothing enforces that a patron may only read their own loans. Denied attempts are not logged; pgAudit records database reads, not denials. Both access denial and recording are only partly covered.
